articles.title: Crypto vs Stocks, Minute by Minute: What 4-5 November Shows About BTC and 24/7 Equity Perps
articles.excerpt: "Bitcoin trades like a tech stock" is usually argued from daily closes. Until recently that was the only honest way to do it: the stock market closed at 16:00 New York time and crypto didn't. Binance…
articles.body: "Bitcoin trades like a tech stock" is usually argued from daily closes. Until recently that was the only honest way to do it: the stock market closed at 16:00 New York time and crypto didn't. Binance now lists USDⓈ-M perpetuals on gold, silver, crude, copper and a dozen US stocks next to BTC and ETH, all trading 24/7 on the same venue. That makes a minute-by-minute comparison possible, in every US session, including weekends. The first week of November gave us a good starting point: 4 November: BTC +2.9% and ETH +5.7%. A basket of 12 US stock perps ended flat (−0.1%), hiding a 14-point spread between MSFT (+6.7%) and MU (−7.0%). 5 November: the stock basket fell 7.8%, a −5.2σ day against its own previous 60 sessions. BTC fell 4.9%, which was only −2.1σ for BTC.

articles.title: Building an open source subscription backend
articles.excerpt: My first attempt to add subscriptions to my app failed, so I built SubTru. SubTru is an open source, self-hostable API that processes subscription events from Stripe, the Apple App Store, and Google P…
articles.body: My first attempt to add subscriptions to my app failed, so I built SubTru. SubTru is an open source, self-hostable API that processes subscription events from Stripe, the Apple App Store, and Google Play. Your app can then call SubTru's GET /access endpoint to fetch any user's subscription status. Below, I discuss some of the challenges I faced and the design decisions I made along the way. It started with disaster I had no idea how challenging adding subscriptions to an app could be. My first attempt at this was a disaster. I had spent months writing the code to handle my users' subscriptions, but all it took was one small misconfiguration for things to break. Long story short, my logic didn't update my customer's subscription status after they made a purchase.

articles.title: Designing a rate limiter: token bucket, sliding window and limits across many servers
articles.excerpt: In short A rate limiter decides, on every request, whether a key (an IP address, a user, an API key or a tenant) is still within its allowance. Token bucket is the usual default because it allows shor…
articles.body: In short A rate limiter decides, on every request, whether a key (an IP address, a user, an API key or a tenant) is still within its allowance. Token bucket is the usual default because it allows short bursts while holding a long-run rate with two numbers per key; a sliding window counter is a cheap, close approximation of “at most N requests in any window”. Across many servers the state lives in a shared store and each decision is one atomic operation, and a client over its limit gets HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header. Key points A fixed window is simple but lets through up to twice the limit across a window boundary. A token bucket has a refill rate, which sets the long-run limit, and a capacity, which sets the largest burst. It stores a token count and a timestamp per key.

They also evaluate the effort, confidence, and time required to complete a purchase. This is where Amazon's growth strategy becomes interesting. Amazon has built its retail experience around a combination of convenience, personalized discovery, competitive value, customer trust, and loyalty .

articles.excerpt: From six minutes of darkness in Egypt or totality over the Australian Outback, here are the pros and cons of the next two total solar eclipses.
articles.body: For those who want to experience a total solar eclipse, the next two years present the best kind of problem. On Aug. 2, 2027, the so-called "eclipse of the century " will sweep across southern Spain, North Africa and the Middle East, bringing more than six minutes of totality to parts of Egypt. Then, on July 22, 2028, another exceptionally long total solar eclipse will cross Australia, putting the remote Outback and Sydney Harbor in the path of the moon's dark central shadow before it reaches New Zealand's beautiful South Island. Both eclipses will be spectacular, and both will require careful planning, yet they promise very different experiences.

articles.body: Twin NASA spacecraft are wrapping up a year-long escapade, ready to make a beeline to the Red Planet. The Escape and Plasma Acceleration and Dynamics Explorers (ESCAPADE) spacecraft launched in November 2025 on the second-ever flight of Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket. But rather than head straight to Mars, the two spacecraft dawdled through a looping trajectory . Now, they are back in Earth's neighborhood where they tackled a crucial engine burn unusually close to Earth that — if all goes well — will set them on track for Mars . "No NASA mission has ever done this before," said Rob Lillis, a planetary and space physicist at the University of California, Berkeley and principal investigator of the ESCAPADE mission.
